analysis.one_liner: NTPC is India's largest power generator, majority-owned by the Government of India, running coal, gas and hydro plants under a cost-plus regulated-equity model while rapidly building out a renewables arm, NTPC Green Energy.
tags: Coal supply row with Coal India
analysis.whats_happening: NTPC has declared a first interim dividend of ₹3 per share for FY27, with the record date on 6 November 2026 - just days away. This follows Q2 FY27 results (announced 31 October 2026) showing consolidated profit up 40.7% YoY to ₹7,351 crore on revenue up 21.2% to ₹54,270 crore. Management also trimmed its FY27 renewable capacity-addition target to 8 GW from 9.5 GW, blaming transmission-grid bottlenecks rather than project delays, and flagged a public dispute with Coal India after its coal stock fell from about 18 million tonnes in April to 5.5 million tonnes in October 2026.
analysis.plain_terms: NTPC gets paid a government-regulated return on the power plants it builds, so its profits move with how much capacity it adds rather than with volatile market power prices - that's why earnings grow steadily instead of swinging wildly. The tension right now: NTPC is chasing an ambitious 149 GW-by-2032 target, mostly renewables, but says the electricity grid can't yet absorb new renewable capacity fast enough, and its own listed renewables arm, NTPC Green Energy, has fallen roughly 31% since its late-2024 listing even as its revenue keeps growing strongly. In short, the growth plan is real, but the market isn't yet convinced the execution and the payoff line up.
analysis.quarters: Consolidated revenue and profit have grown cleanly for two straight quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun-26) revenue ₹50,741 crore/PAT ₹6,896 crore, then Q2 FY27 (Sep-26) revenue ₹54,270 crore (+21.2% YoY)/PAT ₹7,351 crore (+40.7% YoY) - both broad-based, not off a tiny base. One quarter stands out oddly: Q4 FY26 (Mar-26) PAT jumped to ₹10,615 crore from ₹5,597 crore the prior quarter on a smaller revenue base - this looks like a year-end regulatory/deferred-tax true-up typical of regulated utilities rather than a step-change in the core business, but the exact driver is Not verified - check on Screener or NTPC's annual report. Management said the FY27 capacity-addition guidance cut (8 GW vs 9.5 GW planned) reflects transmission-grid constraints, not execution delays, with relief expected only around mid-2027.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 23.3% from its September 2024 peak of ₹421.29, last at ₹323, within a 52-week range of ₹298-₹405.82. NTPC did a 1.2:1 stock split in March 2019 - this is a plain split, not a demerger or spin-off, so it does not understate returns the way a spin-off would; the drawdown is a genuine price decline. Over 1 year the stock is roughly flat (-1.03%) while the Nifty fell 9.01% and peer Tata Power fell 12.36%, so NTPC held up better in a weak market. Over 3 years it has risen 47.57%, in line with the peer (47.95%) and well ahead of the Nifty (21.89%); over 5 years it is up 178.87% against the Nifty's 31.04% and the peer's 61.13% - strong long-run outperformance, though the recent peak-to-trough fall shows that strength has cooled.
analysis.valuation_read: At roughly 10.5x trailing earnings and about 1.45x book value (book value near ₹220/share), NTPC trades well below its own FY24 (15.65x) and FY25 (14.81x) multiples, closer to its FY23 level (10.05x). Why it looks cheap: the market is pricing in the cut capacity-addition guidance, the unresolved transmission-grid bottleneck, and the fresh coal-supply dispute with Coal India. Whether it is actually cheap is less clear-cut: ROE of 15.1% is above its own five-year average of around 13.5% and has been improving each year, so the underlying earnings engine looks healthy - the discount reads more like the market discounting near-term execution risk than a broken business.
analysis.growth_read: Growth here is volume-led and real, not a low-base illusion: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 21.2% YoY and PAT 40.7% YoY, backed by coal plants running at 75.11% plant load factor versus a 68.35% national average. The renewables arm, NTPC Green Energy, grew H1 FY27 revenue 58% YoY and profit 59% YoY, forming the core of NTPC's 149 GW-by-2032 ambition (about 60 GW of which is meant to be renewables). Margins have also held up (EBITDA margin ~28.8% in Q2 FY27 versus ~28.6% a year earlier), so this is growth with margin support, not volume chased at the expense of profitability.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting into dividends reliably - a 34.3% payout ratio and a steady TTM dividend of ₹9/share (2.79% yield), with a fresh ₹3/share interim declared for FY27. ROE stands at 15.1%, but ROCE of 8.92% appears to be a dip from the 10.99% reported for FY25 - Not verified - check on Screener or NTPC's annual report, since it runs against an otherwise improving multi-year trend. Debt/equity of about 1.33x is high in absolute terms but structural for a capital-intensive regulated utility funding a large capex programme, and is reported to be trending down over the past three years - the bigger near-term concern here is business risk (grid bottlenecks, coal supply visibility) rather than financial/balance-sheet risk.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India holds 51.10% as promoter (as of September 2026), with 0% pledging - as expected for a state-controlled utility. FII holding has edged down (from about 16.5% in March 2026 to 15.79% in September 2026) while domestic institutional holding has risen (29.13% to 29.86% over the same period), suggesting domestic funds have absorbed foreign selling. There is no marquee individual or star investor on the shareholding register - this is a government-controlled utility held mainly by institutions, not a stock typically associated with high-profile individual investors. No evidence was found of any government stake sale (OFS) in NTPC during 2026.
strengths: Consolidated PAT grew 40.7% YoY to ₹7,351 crore in Q2 FY27 on revenue growth of 21.2% - a broad-based gain, not a low-base effect
Coal plants run at a 75.11% plant load factor versus a 68.35% national average, showing above-average asset utilisation
ROE of 15.1% sits above its own roughly 13.5% five-year average and has improved steadily since FY22
Dividend track record intact at ₹9/share TTM (2.79% yield, 34.3% payout ratio), with a further ₹3/share interim declared for FY27, record date 6 November 2026
watchpoints: Management cut FY27 renewable capacity-addition guidance to 8 GW from 9.5 GW, citing transmission-grid bottlenecks it says will only ease by mid-2027

Public dispute with Coal India: NTPC's coal stock fell from about 18 million tonnes in April 2026 to 5.5 million tonnes by October, and it plans to buy 10 million tonnes commercially, while Coal India denies any shortfall - an unresolved fuel-security question

Listed subsidiary NTPC Green Energy has fallen roughly 31% since its November 2024 listing despite H1 FY27 revenue growing 58% YoY - a disconnect between the renewables growth story and how the market is pricing it
ROCE of 8.92% looks lower than the 10.99% reported for FY25 - Not verified - check on Screener or NTPC's annual report before relying on this trend
analysis.one_thing: Whether NTPC resolves the transmission-grid bottleneck it says is capping renewable capacity additions, which management expects only around mid-2027 - that single execution point determines whether the 149 GW-by-2032 growth plan stays on schedule.
analysis.data_notes: Quarterly and valuation figures cross-checked against Screener.in and corroborated by IndianPSU.com/Business Standard reporting dated October-November 2026. Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT of ₹7,351 crore was used as the more consistent figure after some sources cited ₹7,029-7,030 crore instead. The ROCE figure (8.92%) could not be reconciled against an apparently higher FY25 figure (10.99%) and was not independently verified against NTPC's own annual report. Two conflicting capex figures (₹7 lakh crore vs ₹16.86 lakh crore) for the 149 GW-by-2032 plan were found in press coverage and neither was used in this report since they could not be reconciled. No confirmed Q3 FY27 results date or 2026 government stake-sale (OFS) could be verified.
